national.summary: A Russian drone hit two trains at a station in central Ukraine, killing at least 14 people, but a local truce credited to Melania Trump is bringing some hope elsewhere.
national.body: Kherson, Ukraine — A jet-powered Russian drone hit two passenger trains stopped at a station in Dnipro in central Ukraine Thursday, killing at least 14 people and injuring 14 more, including a 40-year-old man whose legs were amputated, officials said. A Russian cruise missile killed two 15-year-old girls in the northern city of Chernihiv, meanwhile, and three more civilians died when a Russian drone hit an apartment block in the central city of Kremenchuk, Ukrainian authorities said. In all, 56 people were injured in the strikes, including 10 children, as Russia continued its deadly attacks on civilians even as a localized ceasefire credited by both sides to U.S. first lady Melania Trump held in the stricken city of Oleshky.Humanitarian aid was poised to roll into Oleshky, a Ukrainian official said Thursday, as the limited ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine stretched into a third day and military units cleared away landmines. Moscow and Kyiv have observed the truce in and around the devastated southern Ukrainian city since Tuesday, but the neighboring nations remain otherwise locked in the war that began with Russia's full-scale invasion more than 4 ½ years ago. Previous efforts to secure ceasefires either never worked out or the truces quickly fell apart. Russia's Defense Ministry said air defenses downed 1,214 Ukrainian drones overnight in one of the largest drone attacks launched by Kyiv. Around half of the drones were heading to the Russian capital, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said. The planned six-day ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky has brought a rare and welcome stillness for civilians in the nearby city of Kherson, which is held by Ukraine and has also been wracked by the war. Both sides thanked Melania Trump for what the White House said was her role in helping broker the temporary ceasefire so food and medical supplies can be delivered to some 2,000 desperate people trapped in Oleshky. national.title: Alaska governor orders probe into Democratic campaign's alleged links to same-name candidate
national.summary: The Republican governor was responding to allegations in the New York Times that Democrats recruited a spoiler candidate, Dan Sullivan.
national.body:
The Republican governor of Alaska has ordered an investigation into an alleged "scheme" which led to two Dan Sullivans standing in the state's US Senate race.

Governor Mike Dunleavy said he was responding to a New York Times (NYT) story , external which said the team of Democratic candidate Mary Peltola worked with people who tried to recruit spoiler candidates in the Senate race.

The governor's post on X said he would investigate "whether this scheme violated Alaska's laws". He did not say which laws he had in mind.

Dan Sullivan, the incumbent Republican senator running for re-election, and allies have accused the Democrats of trying to confuse voters. Peltola's team deny any wrongdoing.

They say they did not encourage the second Dan Sullivan, a retired teacher who lives in a remote fishing village, to stand. He has denied any links with the Peltola campaign.

The Alaska race is considered by analysts to be one of the tightest of the upcoming US midterm elections, which will decide which party controls Congress. Americans head to the polls across the country on Tuesday.

Dunleavy's statement, which did not name the Peltola campaign, said the NYT reporting had supported findings by the state Division of Elections earlier this year.

"I am therefore directing the Department of Public Safety to investigate whether this scheme violated Alaska's laws and whether criminal charges or civil action are warranted," he wrote. "The evidence will determine what happens next."

national.title: Inflation heats up again, days before midterm elections
national.summary: Rising gas prices drove much of the inflation increase as renewed violence in the Middle East has kept oil prices above $100 a barrel, up from below $70 before the Iran war. But prices also rose outside of fuel costs.
national.body:
Christopher Rugaber, Associated Press Christopher Rugaber, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — An inflation gauge closely monitored by the Federal Reserve accelerated last month, showing that prices remain elevated less than a week before midterm elections in which the uncomfortably high cost of living for millions of Americans has become a central issue.

Consumer prices rose 3.6% in September from a year earlier, the Commerce Department said Thursday, up from 3.4% in August. On a monthly basis, prices climbed 0.5%, up from 0.3% in August and the highest figure since May.

Rising gas prices drove much of the inflation increase as renewed violence in the Middle East has kept oil prices above $100 a barrel, up from below $70 before the Iran war. But prices also rose outside of fuel costs. The cost of services such as shipping, hotel rooms, and utilities increased rapidly from August to September, a sign that inflation is spreading and growing more entrenched.

"The inflation outlook has become more concerning," Ksenia Bushmeneva, an economist at TD, a bank, wrote in a commentary on the report. "Price pressures are showing signs of heating up. Elevated gasoline prices are keeping headline inflation hot, but underlying pressures are also broadening."

WATCH: Warsh holds briefing after Fed leaves key interest rate unchanged

Polls show that the rise in inflation has soured most voters on the economy, leading them to give President Donald Trump poor marks on handling rising prices. Trump campaigned in 2024 on lowering the cost of living, including bringing the cost of gas below $2 a gallon. It currently averages about $4.25 a gallon nationwide.

Excluding the volatile energy and food categories, core inflation also picked up last month. It increased 3.1% from a year ago in September, up from 3% in August, the Commerce Department said. And from August to September, core prices rose 0.3%, the same as the previous month.

national.title: US and Japan agree to establish a Japanese facility for joint missile production
national.summary: The announcement Wednesday is the latest action by the allies, who have repeatedly expressed alarm over China's growing assertiveness in Asia.
national.body:
From left, Philippines Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro, Australia Defense Minister Richard Marles, Japan Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and U.S.Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth prepare to leave after posing for pictures before holding a Quadrilateral Meeting on the sidelines of the 20th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Defence Ministers' Meeting (ADMM) and 13th ADMM-Plus Meetings in Cebu, Philippines, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. Rolex Dela Pena/Pool EPA via AP hide caption

CEBU, Philippines — The United States and Japan have agreed to establish a Japanese facility for the joint production of advanced medium-range air-to-air missiles, the Japanese defense chief said.

It is the latest move by the allies, which have repeatedly expressed alarm over China's growing assertiveness in Asia.

Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi made the announcement in a news conference Wednesday night in the central Philippine province of Cebu, where he met U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on the sidelines of an annual meeting of Southeast Asian defense chiefs and their major Asian and Western counterparts.

Koizumi raised concern Thursday about China's increasing naval activity in southwestern Japan. He said that three Chinese destroyers and a coast guard ship together crossed the Osumi Strait south of the southern main island of Kyushu and headed east to the Pacific Ocean this week. It was the first such fleet configuration his ministry has spotted, he said.

Koizumi said he cited the incident as "an example illustrating the challenging security environment in the region" in his remark at a session Thursday. His ministry will keep watching the Chinese activity with high level of interest, he said. Japan has been accelerating military buildup in southwestern Japan to deter China.

The annual meetings aim to avert a major regional conflict and strengthen defense cooperation. On the sidelines of the meetings, however, the U.S. and China and their allies have often traded criticisms.

The missiles that will be produced as part of a joint effort called "Operation Supercharge" are essential for the F-35 fighter jets, Koizumi said. The two sides agreed to build a final assembly and inspection plant for the Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile, or AMRAAM, in Japan, he said. The U.S.-made F-35s are one of the world's most advanced aircraft and are also used by the Japanese military.

national.title: China elevates a military general to the Politburo and seeks to strengthen party discipline
national.summary: This move comes about a year before President Xi Jinping is expected to secure his fourth five-year term.
national.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping, center left and Zhang Shengmin, Vice Chairman of the Central Military Commission second from right attend a ceremony in honor of fallen national heroes at the Monument to the People's Heroes to mark Martyrs' Day at Tiananmen Square in Beijing, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026. Ng Han Guan/AP hide caption

BANGKOK — China's top leaders on Thursday elevated the only remaining general on the commission that oversees the country's military to the Politburo, the top governing body of the Communist Party.

The leaders also adopted a resolution on strengthening self-governance, discipline and anti-corruption in the party, as they seek to extend their grip on power.

During a four-day closed-door meeting, top Communist Party leaders deliberated on and adopted resolutions that will guide the party in the coming years. The meeting comes about a year before President Xi Jinping is widely expected to secure his fourth five-year term as the party's leader.

The party elected Gen. Zhang Shengmin, who currently serves as vice chairman of the Central Military Commission, to the Politburo. Xi had earlier purged two of China's top generals, leaving Zhang as the commission's only member besides Xi himself. It also left the Politburo without any representatives from the People's Liberation Army.

Zhang also holds a position overseeing internal discipline for the military, serving as deputy secretary of the CMC Commission for Discipline Inspection.

The party said in a summary of the resolution that the tasks facing it were "increasingly arduous," such as "uniting and leading the people to safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests."

It said it must step up its self-governance, which involves rooting out corruption and maintaining ideological purity.

national.title: U.S. economy grows at brisk 3.4% pace in third quarter on strong consumer spending and AI investment
national.summary: Consumer spending rose at a good clip in the third quarter, and business investment was up sharply, reflecting the AI boom.
national.body:
Paul Wiseman, Associated Press Paul Wiseman, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — The U.S. economy grew at a healthy 3.4% annual pace from July through September, accelerating from the second quarter on strong consumer spending and investment in artificial intelligence.

The expansion in third-quarter gross domestic product – the nation's output of goods and services – was faster than the 2.2% growth registered from April through June, the Commerce Department said Thursday. Consumer spending rose at a brisk 3.8% clip in the third quarter, and business investment was up sharply, reflecting the AI boom.

The American economy – by far, the world's biggest – has proven resilient in the face of higher energy prices caused by the fighting with Iran.

Economists had expected GDP to grow 3% in the third quarter, according to a survey of forecasters by the data firm FactSet.

U.S. growth has been lifted by an AI investment boom. Business investment, excluding housing, was up 12.7% in the third quarter. Investment in information processing equipment surged 37.4%, in software 9.6% and in research and development 7.5%.

However, housing investment, hurt by high mortgage rates, dropped 3.3% and has now fallen six of the last seven quarters.

Thursday's report was the first of three Commerce Department estimates of third-quarter GDP growth.

national.title: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
national.summary: With 99% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its allies are set to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.
national.body:
Partial results from Israel's general election show veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu marginally ahead of his rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, but still short of a majority in parliament.

With 99% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies were on track to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc were set for 48.

Both leaders have said they will try to form a governing coalition.

Arab-led parties, which are on course to win an unprecedented 19 seats, could emerge as kingmakers. But all but one of the Jewish parties have pledged not to work with them.

On Thursday, officials began counting as many as 480,000 absentee ballots from groups including soldiers, diplomats and hospital patients, who could not get to polling stations.

These votes may change the final number of seats allotted to each party under Israel's proportional representation system.

Once the results are confirmed, President Isaac Herzog will hold consultations with all the political factions and invite the leader whom he believes has the best chance of success to form a government - a process that could take weeks.

If they fail, then ultimately there would have to be another election.

national.title: EU chief lays out vision for new Canada partnership at Montreal summit
national.summary: Ursula von der Leyen continued to use the term "associate member" for Canada despite some opposition of the bloc's members, including Germany.
national.body:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has laid out her vision for what an "associate membership" status for Canada to the EU would look like as officials gather in Montreal to discuss closer ties.

It is "a partnership that comes close to membership than anything we have done before," she said on Thursday's remarks at the two-day Canada-EU summit.

She added it is a type of relationship that would be open "only to our closest partners outside of Europe who are ready to open a new frontier together."

It includes close alignment on governance and policies, and partnering in research and innovation.

For decades, Canada-EU summits took place without much fanfare - but that's not the case for this year's meeting in the Canadian city.

Thursday and Friday's summit is being closely watched for details on how Canada and the European bloc deepen their ties.

Von der Leyen first proposed "opening the door" to Canada last month for what she called an "associate membership" - a status that does not currently exist.

The overture came after Prime Minister Carney addressed the European Parliament in Strasbourg, telling EU lawmakers that Canada and Europe were "stronger together" in the face of "geopolitical rupture".

national.title: DoorDash to buy Instacart in $17bn deal it says will expand customer options
national.summary: Instacart shoppers will be able to buy from 150,000 stores, compared to the 100,000 currently available on the platform, the firms said.
national.body:
DoorDash will acquire grocery delivery firm Instacart in a $17bn (£12.8bn) deal, creating a behemoth that will bring more meals, quick-need purchases and big weekly shops directly to customers.

DoorDash said the deal, expected to be final in about a year, will expand options for customers and let more sellers use the companies' services.

Instacart shoppers will be able to buy from 150,000 stores, up from the current 100,000, while DoorDash will reach beyond restaurants into retail, the firms said.

"Together, we can accelerate innovation across the grocery industry and make online grocery more seamless and affordable for the millions of households we serve," Instacart's chief executive said.

"Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more," CEO Chris Rogers also said.

For DoorDash, the acquisition will allow it to use Instacart's grocery selection and substitution expertise, the company's co-founder and chief executive, Tony Xu, said.

"Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online. Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you'd choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts," Xu said.

He added that "Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day".

national.title: Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself 'leader of Brazil' after election loss
national.summary: The defeated presidential candidate says he will lead the opposition from the US.
national.body:
The defeated candidate in Brazil's presidential election, Flávio Bolsonaro, has referred to himself as "leader of Brazil" in a letter he published on social media after leaving the country for the United States.

Bolsonaro lost to his left-wing rival, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, in the run-off on Sunday by a difference of 4.4 million votes, but has not conceded defeat.

In the letter, Bolsonaro alleges, without offering evidence, that he was the victim of "electoral fraud" and says that he will lead the opposition from the US.

He left Brazil on Tuesday after failing to comply with an order to surrender his passports, a decision which Lula described as "a shameful act".

Bolsonaro starts his letter, which he posted on his X account, saying "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the leader of Brazil".

However, he had posted a previous version, that was later deleted, in which he wrote: "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the rightful president of Brazil."

Both versions repeat the allegation that Bolsonaro first made on election night, that an extension of polling hours on Sunday had benefited his rival.

In the letter, he says it was "an electoral fraud unfolding before my eyes".

national.title: Greetings from Baghdad, where Agatha Christie's old home presents its own mystery
national.summary: The English writer visited Iraq multiple times in the first half of the 20th century and set some of her mystery novels there. The house in Baghdad where she once lived now sits abandoned and crumbling.
national.body:
Jane Arraf/NPR This, according to Iraq's culture ministry, is the one-time home of English mystery novelist Agatha Christie, on the banks of the Tigris River in Baghdad.

Fittingly, the abandoned house has its own mystery: why it's been left to decay over the last century.

Christie made dozens of trips to Iraq, including the one where she met her archaeologist husband, Max Mallowan, in 1930. They Came to Baghdad and Murder in Mesopotamia were two of her novels set in Iraq.

As for the house, it's a heritage property controlled by Iraq's culture ministry. The Iraqi government says it's willing to make the house available to anyone who will restore it. It is padlocked and literally falling down.

When we visited this month, there was a $200 electricity bill stuffed into a hole in the door — apparently reflecting years of unpaid bills in its more recent history.

national.title: Alaska's governor orders a probe into Peltola's Senate campaign over spoiler candidate controversy
national.summary: Republican Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy has ordered an investigation into the Democratic candidate running for the U.S. Senate in the state after revelations that her campaign appeared to be involved in recruiting another candidate with the same name as Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan.
national.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Republican Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy has ordered an investigation into the Democratic candidate running for the U.S. Senate in the state after revelations that her campaign appeared to be involved in recruiting another candidate with the same name as Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan.

Dunleavy's order, posted overnight on social media, comes a day after President Donald Trump called for the criminal prosecution of Mary Peltola and her campaign.

In a race that's among a handful of Senate contests this year expected to determine control of the chamber, the Republican president had previously directed his Department of Justice to sue to block certification of it, demanding that Alaska be prevented from certifying a win by Peltola if Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. remains on the state's ballots.

Dunleavy wrote that reporting by The New York Times "reveals disturbing new evidence of an organized effort to manipulate Alaska's elections by recruiting candidates — including one with the same name as an incumbent U.S. Senator — to deliberately confuse voters and misdirect their votes."

WATCH: Trump calls for Peltola to drop out after report her campaign helped recruit 2nd Dan Sullivan

"Deliberately tricking voters into casting their ballots for someone else strikes at the integrity of our elections," Dunleavy added, noting that the reporting "substantially supports" earlier findings by the state's elections board into the matter.

Peltola's campaign didn't immediately respond to a message early Thursday seeking comment on Dunleavy's order. But during a campaign stop in Soldotna, Peltola, a former congresswoman, suggested the Times' report was a "distraction" from issues such as Sen. Sullivan's support of the war in Iran.

"This is just another distraction. It's another diversion," she said in a video posted online. "This is all stuff to sell newspapers. This is all stuff to get subscriptions."

national.body:
At least 14 people have been killed after a Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro, local officials have said.

Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 14 others were wounded in the attack, including an 11-year-old boy.

Ukraine's state railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, said a passenger train headed for the southern city of Zaporizhzhia was at one of the platforms in Dnipro when the drone hit.

Russia's military has not publicly commented. It has repeatedly hit Ukraine's large railway network, but Moscow denies deliberately targeting civilians.

In Dnipro, an elevated threat level was announced ahead of Thursday's strike, according to the railway operator chief, Oleksandr Pertsovsky.

"But unfortunately there were still a large number of people on the platform" when the drone struck, he said.

Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov said the incident was a tragedy, adding that a drone hit an electric civilian train.

Pictures from the Ukrainian rescue services show a large hole in a platform that is strewn with blurred-out bodies, near a blast-damaged train with smashed windows.

national.summary: One of the region's famous rock formations, known as "fairy chimneys", reportedly collapsed outside an open-air museum.
national.body:
At least two people have been killed and five injured after a rock formation collapsed at a tourist site in Turkey's historical region of Cappadocia, local media is reporting.

One of the rock spires, which are known as fairy chimneys, reportedly disintegrated at the popular open-air museum in the central town of Göreme.

Nevşehir provincial Governor Hüseyin Kök said the victims' bodies had been recovered from under the rubble, but the justice minister warned there could be "other potential victims" still trapped.

The cause of Thursday's incident was not immediately known, however local media reported the collapse could have been triggered by heavy rain.

Turkish media reported that the collapse happened near the entrance to the museum - a UNESCO World Heritage site - at about 15:15 local time (12:15 GMT).

In a later post on social media, Justice Minister Akın Gürlek said that "according to initial assessments, two individuals have lost their lives in the incident, and five others have been injured".

He added that a search and rescue operation was continuing at the site.

The Cappadocia region attracts tourists from around the world, who want to see the ancient fairy chimneys - tall, cone-shaped rock formations that are created by volcanic activity.

national.body: Two astronauts stepped outside the International Space Station Thursday for the first of two spacewalks, one week apart, to install a final pair of roll-out solar blankets that will complete a complex, years-long upgrade of the lab's aging power system.Floating in the station's Quest airlock, NASA's Anil Menon and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk switched their suits to battery power at 7:57 a.m. EDT, officially kicking off a planned six-and-a-half-hour spacewalk, the eighth so far this year and the 285th since ISS assembly began in 1998.The spacewalk began in orbital darkness, prompting Kutryk to observe "the night is dark and full of wonders."The goal of the excursion and a follow-on spacewalk next week is to complete an upgrade that began in 2021 when the first of eight ISS roll-out solar arrays, or IROSAs, was installed. The IROSAs are smaller than the station's original solar panels but they are more efficient, featuring state-of-the-art solar cells.Before the first IROSA was installed, the original arrays were generating about 152 kilowatts of power. The six IROSAs installed to date have boosted that up to about 200 kilowatts. Philippine police have obtained a warrant to examine devices seized from the former home of Thomas Markle, father of the Duchess of Sussex.

Earlier this month, it was reported that hundreds of images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Thomas Markle Sr, 82, had been found at the property in the Philippines.

Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old videotapes, were handed to police by Meghan's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, last week. However, officers in Cebu needed a court warrant before they could examine the items.

Thomas Markle Sr, who is now in the US, has strongly denied the allegations made by his son, describing them as "sick lies".

Cebu Regional Prosecutor Graeme Elmido told the BBC that Thomas Markle Jr was "adamant" that the case should be investigated, and that he felt his father "has to answer for it".

Last week, the Sun on Sunday reported that Thomas Markle Sr's ex-wife, Roslyn Loveless, had sent a letter to the Metropolitan Police about the 2019 allegations, which was shared with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex at the time.

Loveless, who has since died, is the mother of Meghan's two half-siblings. She divorced Thomas Markle Sr. in 1975, before he married the duchess's mother.

The duchess has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.

national.summary: The U.S. central bank left borrowing costs unchanged this month after hiking rates in September for the first time in three years.
national.body: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady on Wednesday after hiking borrowing costs in September to clamp down on inflation. The central bank left the federal funds rate at a target range of 3.75% to 4%, keeping it unchanged after raising rates last month for the first time in three years.In a statement, the Fed said economic activity is growing at a "strong pace" while acknowledging that inflation remains elevated. "The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2% goal," Fed officials said. Wall Street had forecast that the Fed would stand pat on rates. Investor reaction was muted, with the three major indexes remaining essentially flat after the Fed's announcement. The Fed's benchmark rate is its main weapon for stabilizing consumer prices, which have crept up in recent months. The latest rate decision comes less than a week before Americans head to the polls for the midterm elections, where affordability issues will be top of mind for voters. President Trump has long urged the Fed to ease borrowing costs.Stubborn inflation During a press conference after the rate decision, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said economic indicators are moving in the right direction, citing robust consumer spending, a low unemployment rate and healthy overall economic growth.He also said credit conditions — the terms lenders set for borrowing — have tightened for businesses and households since the Fed's September rate hike, a sign the economy is heading toward a "more durable period" of growth and price stability.At the same time, he said inflation remains "too high" and acknowledged that the Fed hasn't yet succeeded in bringing inflation under control. "On the employment side of the Fed's dual mandate, conditions are quite positive, and yet Americans, of course, are still dealing with inflation that has been running above the committee's objective for close to six years," he told reporters. "It's our responsibility to get inflation down."Two dissentsTen members of the Federal Open Market Committee, which sets interest rates, voted to hold the benchmark rate steady. national.title: With days to go before the midterms, data shows the U.S. economy is doing well
national.summary: GDP grew at an annual rate of 3.4% in the third quarter in the last major read on the economy ahead of the midterm elections — but many Americans continue to struggle with affordability.
national.body:
The U.S. economy grew faster in the summer compared to the spring, driven by consumer spending as well as investments in AI.

The Sunday Story Pinching pennies, casting ballots: a midterms dispatch from the Midwest Gross domestic product, which broadly measures economic activity, grew at an annual rate of 3.4% July through September, according to a report from the Commerce Department released Thursday. The previous quarter GDP grew at a 2.2% annual pace.

A big driver for GDP growth in the third quarter was the strong investments from AI companies, which continue to build out data centers and spend big money in developing the technology.

Meanwhile, consumer spending was another of the big drivers of GDP growth, led in part by higher-income Americans who are better able to withstand stubbornly high inflation.

The sturdy GDP data comes just days before the midterm elections, with many Americans saying they feel gloomy about the economy as inflation jacks up the costs of many day-to-day necessities, while the ongoing conflict with Iran drives up energy costs like gasoline.

Although consumer spending has been growing steadily, it has not spread out evenly across households, with lower-income Americans struggling more than high-earners. Wage growth has also fallen behind inflation, further squeezing many Americans.

Siri Steven, a manager at a resale store in Decorah, Iowa, says she and her husband are putting off fixing up their more than 130-year-old house.

"We barely go out to eat now," Steven said. "I really have to be mindful of our budget and make sure that we can pay all our bills and not overdraft."

national.title: Record number of purges as Xi emphasises 'party discipline' at China political gathering
national.summary: Xi's anti-corruption campaign has become "an effort to consolidate and maintain authority", observers say.
national.body:
A record 33 members have been expelled from China's Communist Party as it concluded a major annual political gathering, which had the most empty seats ever seen.

The fifth plenum was attended by 279 Central Committee members, compared to 315 at the fourth plenum in October 2025 and 364 at the third one in July 2024.

While recent plenums focused on economic reforms or social and development issues, party discipline took centre stage at this week's gathering.

Xi Jinping has made the fight against corruption a central pillar of his rule since he took the reins in 2012, calling it the "biggest threat" to the party.

Sixteen of the 33 members expelled are from the military, according to a communique issued on Thursday, which marked the end of the four-day closed-door gathering held at a hotel in Beijing.

It's unclear what specific charges these members face beyond "serious disciplinary and legal violations". Such broad allegations have become routine under Xi's anti-corruption campaign.

It has now become "an effort to consolidate and maintain authority", says Chong Ja Ian, a non-resident scholar with Carnegie China.

"In this case, the campaign will continue and expand depending on how secure Xi feels rather than any real issue with corruption."

Water samples were collected Thursday morning in Fredonia, putting the village on the path to ending its boil order.

The village Office of Emergency Management announced the news in an update at 10:50 a.m.

"Good news: Treated water, turbidity level levels have improved and stabilized, allowing the first steps of samples to be collected this morning," the update stated.

A second set of samples will be collected Friday morning. The county health department lab will analyze the samples, with results expected Saturday morning. "At that time, a determination will be made to either lift or continue the boil order."

The Office of Emergency Management announced separately on Wednesday that a very limited supply of bottled water is available at the Fredonia Fire Department. Water will be rationed for those with the greatest need. It's intended for residents who can’t safely boil water or acquire bottled water.

People interested in getting water should call the fire department's non-emergency line at 672-2125, then press option 1 when prompted.

local.title: Jewish Federation's Gebell appointed to Holocaust memorial commission
local.summary: The 19-member commission will guide the creation of a New York State Holocaust Memorial at the Empire State Plaza in Albany.
local.body:
Gov. Kathy Hochul has appointed Monica Gebell, senior director of the Jewish Federation of Greater Rochester's Center for Advocacy and Education, to the state's Holocaust Memorial Advisory Commission.

The 19-member commission will guide the creation of a New York State Holocaust Memorial at the Empire State Plaza in Albany. Members will help shape the vision of the memorial, its educational goals, and commemorative elements, according to a news release from the federation.

The memorial, according to the release, will commemorate the 6 million Jewish people killed during the Holocaust and millions of other victims of Nazi persecution. It'll also serve "as a site of remembrance and resistance against antisemitism and all forms of hate."

local.title: Trooper shoots man who allegedly pointed a gun at him during a traffic stop
local.summary: It happened in Sodus late Wednesday afternoon.
local.body:
State and Wayne County authorities are investigating an incident where a trooper shot a man during a traffic stop in Sodus.

The trooper initiated the traffic stop at 5:08 p.m. Wednesday on Preemption Road, according to the state police. A records check reportedly showed that the driver, who state police have not identified, had outstanding warrants on burglary and robbery charges, and a Wayne County deputy then responded to the scene.

The trooper approached the vehicle again and attempted to take the driver into custody, but he allegedly refused to exit the vehicle, according to police. He then drove forward with the officer partially inside the vehicle. Police allege that the man then took out a handgun and pointed it at the trooper, and the trooper fired his service pistol, striking him.

The driver was transported to Strong Memorial Hospital by Mercy Flight and was listed in critical but stable condition as of late Wednesday. The trooper was not injured.

local.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) -- The small-ball Milwaukee Brewers playing in the smallest market in the majors are World Series champions for the first time.

Hey, Milwaukee: grab a brat, raise a beer and prepare for that parade.

Young ace Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings, rookie Cooper Pratt had two more hits and two RBIs, and the Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday night to set off a long-awaited celebration among thousands of Brewers fans in attendance at Tropicana Field.

“It’s the best feeling ever. All of our fans are here. I know the city’s waited a long, long time for this,” Milwaukee captain Christian Yelich said. “We’re so happy to bring it home to them. I can’t wait to get back there and celebrate.”

World Series MVP William Contreras hit an RBI double and Misiorowski allowed just two hits before leaving the game because of a right calf cramp. He got a standing ovation from the Brew-Crew fans, who took over the section behind Milwaukee’s dugout for the last three games.

The 22-year-old Pratt set a Series rookie record with six straight hits before a sacrifice fly in the sixth. Jackson Chourio set a five-game Series record with 11 hits.

“This is one of the greatest moments of my life. Oh my gosh. It doesn’t even feel real,” said Pratt, who made his major league debut in June. “This is surreal. It only took four months!”

The championship comes in the 58th season for a franchise that began as the Seattle Pilots in 1969 and moved to Milwaukee the following year. The Brewers’ only previous trip to the World Series in 1982 ended in heartbreak when they blew a 3-1 lead in the sixth inning of Game 7 and lost 6-3 to the St. Louis Cardinals.

local.title: Uprising in France worth U.S. attention
local.summary: For many of us the news stories about the riots that have broken out in French cities are just another story on news channels overwhelmed by stories about Iran, the midterm elections and the price of gasoline. I was like that myself, only wondering why French youth were so upset with their schools.
local.body:
For many of us the news stories about the riots that have broken out in French cities are just another story on news channels overwhelmed by stories about Iran, the midterm elections and the price of gasoline. I was like that myself, only wondering why French youth were so upset with their schools. But as the violence and size of the demonstrations increased with the presence of far left and Islamist groups I began to pay more attention, and I didn't like what I saw.

As I write this not only are Paris, Marseille and other cities in France again experiencing far left and Islamist led demonstrations, but so are cities in Italy including Milan and Rome. Demonstrations are also taking place in Madrid, Lisbon, Athens, Dublin and in cities in Albania, Serbia and Belgium that are mostly led by student groups protesting a variety of local issues like housing shortages, and government corruption. But even in most of those cases leftist and Islamist groups are at work on the fringes.

The riots in France began as high school and university student demonstrations protesting severe underfunding, dilapidated facilities, overcrowded classrooms, and teacher shortages in French public schools. One factor stands out for what precipitated these protests over the shortcomings in the French education system is that spending on France's bloated welfare state for social welfare programs, pensions and healthcare accounts for 59% of its annual budget, the largest of any nation on Earth, while only 10% is spent on education.

To pay for this system of social welfare, France has among the highest tax rates in the western world. Employer social security contributions average 45% of gross salary, while employee contributions vary from 22% to 25%. The tax on consumer goods is 20%. These taxes are a burden on taxpayers but in France over 50% of households pay no tax so that while benefiting from the system they have no hand in the game. By comparison in socialist Denmark everyone pays some tax.

France's financial woes have been further strained by an influx of illegal immigrants, and asylum seekers primarily from Sub-Saharan Central and West Africa, and the Horn of Africa. Those granted Asylum seeker status receive an allowance with a housing supplement if they cannot be housed in a reception center, have immediate comprehensive access to the French health insurance system and even receive discounts on public transportation. Undocumented aliens receive only medical aid, emergency care, and their children can attend French public schools but even those things cost the French government.

local.body:
Through exploration and hands-on learning, children ages 5-10 can join Audubon Community Nature Center's (ACNC) new Nature Connections. This monthly program is offered with homeschooled students and families in mind, though others are welcome.

Beginning Wednesday, from 1 to 2 p.m. on the first Wednesdays of the month Audubon invites 5-10-year-olds to experience a hands-on and exploratory-based approach to learn about the wonders of the natural world.

ACNC Nature Educator Taylor Spontaneo is leading Nature Connections. As she describes, "Audubon is hoping to provide homeschooled children with the experience of connecting with one another as well as a guided hands-on exploration of the natural world. By letting nature be the teacher, children are encouraged to be curious and adventurous in their own way."

Each month will feature a different theme. November's theme is "Hiking Tips and Tricks." Children will learn how to use a map while navigating trails, practice identifying poison ivy vines, and discover many other skills that make a great hiker and explorer.

Children should be dressed to be indoors and outdoors, as the program will take place in both settings. Parents and guardians may drop children off, or adults are welcome to stay.

Participation is $9 for children ages 5-10, $6.75 for Nature Center members. Reservations are appreciated by calling (716) 569-2345 or going to AudubonCNC.org/hiking-tips-and-tricks. Walk-ins are welcome.

Audubon Community Nature Center is located at 1600 Riverside Road, one-quarter mile east of Route 62 between Jamestown, N.Y., and Warren, Pa. You can visit the nearly 600-acre nature preserve, check in on the live birds of prey, enjoy the Nature Play Area, and hike six miles of trails dawn until dusk daily for free.

The three-story Nature Center building houses interactive displays, live animals, the indoor Nature Play Area, the Ralph Simpson Bird Collection, and the Blue Heron Gift Shop. Visitors are welcome Mondays through Saturdays, 10 a.m.-4:30 p.m., and Sundays, 1-4:30 p.m. Nature Center members and SNAP/EBT and Arts Access cardholders have free building admission daily. Building admission is also free Sundays for non-Nature Center members.

local.title: Hochul signs domestic violence, human trafficking bills
local.summary: Gov. Kathy Hochul has signed three bills into law as Domestic Violence Awareness Month winds down. Hochul on Tuesday signed A.10960A/S.9671, which requires local Boards of Election to notify survivors at least six months in advance of their protection expiring. Such notice will remind survivors of t
local.body:
Gov. Kathy Hochul has signed three bills into law as Domestic Violence Awareness Month winds down.

Hochul on Tuesday signed A.10960A/S.9671, which requires local Boards of Election to notify survivors at least six months in advance of their protection expiring. Such notice will remind survivors of the date their protection will end and the process for filing a new request to ensure the continued confidentiality of their records.

The legislation was sponsored by Assemblywoman Linda Rosenthal, D-Manhattan, and Sen. Michelle Hinchey, D-Kingston.

"Stalking, harassment and the many other abusive tactics used by perpetrators of domestic violence often continue long after a survivor has left the situation," Rosenthal said. "The signing of this legislation will ensure that a survivor's address information can be kept private by the Board of Elections for as long as necessary, ensuring confidentiality and protecting their safety."

Under current law, domestic violence survivors can file a request with their local Board of Elections to keep their voter registration record, including their address, confidential. Any survivor at risk of physical or emotional harm to themselves or their family may apply for the four-year protection, but there is no requirement that survivors be warned before that protection expires, leaving their information vulnerable once again if they do not renew it. .

"Survivors may spend years rebuilding their lives after escaping an abusive situation," Rosenthal said. "With so much going on, it can be easy to forget to renew this crucial protection, underscoring the importance of receiving advance notice from the Board of Elections. With a simple notice, survivors will be empowered to renew these protections, shielding their addresses from those who wish to do harm."

The legislation was approved unanimously in the state Assembly and Senate.

"We must use every tool possible to ensure that survivors of domestic violence remain safe and can feel secure in their lives," Hinchey said. "Requiring the state Board of Elections to notify survivors before their confidential voter registration status expires will help prevent a lapse in this critical layer of protection. I'm proud to sponsor this legislation, and I thank Assemblymember Linda Rosenthal for her partnership in getting this done and Governor Hochul for signing it into law so that we can strengthen an important safeguard for New Yorkers."

Deborah A. Fisher age 77 of Gowanda passed away Friday afternoon October 23, 2026 surrounded by family and love.

Deborah was born in Buffalo, NY on December 9, 1948 the daughter of LeRoy and Helen (Cocoran) Goodley.

After graduating high school Deb went onto nursing school, her career as a Registered Nurse started in 1969 and spanned 35 years . She worked at the former Tri-County Hospital, Gowanda, the former Lakeshore Hospital in Irving, she retired from the former Gowanda Psychiatric Center.

Deb was a devoted mom, she loved her family, followed her faith and treasured friendships throughout her life.

Survivors include her children ; Joseph (Charity) Sweda of Gowanda, Tara (Miguel) Sanchez of Gowanda. Grandchildren; Jace , Samuel and Hunter. She shared her life with John Fisher for 20 years, John and his children Annie, Scott and Kellye and their families also survive as does her brother, Robert (Genevieve) Goodley.

OBSERVER Photo by Christian Storms North Collins’ Gage Mathis clears a ball from Maple Grove’s JT Sellstrom during the first half of the Section VI Class D championship on Wednesday night at Hamburg High School.

HAMBURG -- After two matchups in the regular season, splitting wins in Chautauqua-Cattaraugus Athletic Association Division III, the North Collins and Maple Grove boys soccer teams were well prepared for each other in the Section VI Class D final Wednesday night at Hamburg High School.

Tied through the first 68 minutes, the game looked like it would be heading to overtime with the contest scoreless. Then in the 69th minute, North Collins sent a cross through the box and contact going after the ball saw the Eagles awarded a penalty kick.

North Collins leading scorer Neven Sheehy made no mistake from the mark and fired home the only goal of the contest to secure the Class D title.

"It's nice to get back here," North Collins head coach Jay Walters said about winning the sectional title. "Maple Grove is a great team, they came at us with such speed. We played them twice this year and split. We played them on turf, we played them on grass. They were fast, they were physically aggressive tonight. It was a really nice contest to be a part of."

Maple Grove did not ruminate on the disappointment of the penalty call and instead began pressing as hard as it had all night for a goal.

"After a four-year break, coming back I am so proud that it's these boys," Maple Grove head coach Cara Abbey stated. "I'm so proud of them, I'm thankful for them. They know how to fight, they know how to go to war with each other and there is no better group of guys to win with or lose with."

local.body:
I've been a Milky Way girl since I was five.With Halloween just around the corner, I have a mini-excuse for having my forbidden goodies in the house. The other 51 weeks a year, I can't risk even bringing them onto the property - the temptation is too strong,

In my hometown, a little mom-and-pop store - Murphy's - was directly across the street from my school. Not many days went by that I didn't stop in for my nickel Milky Way "fix." Oh yes, there was the rare Sugar Daddy or handful of Double Bubble, but mostly I stuck to the old tried and true. In later years I learned to eat Milky Ways frozen. They lasted longer that way, but I'm really amazed I still have my teeth.

I don't think I've ever bought Halloween candy without Milky Ways in the mix. These days, I'll have to admit that Butterfingers are running a close second with an occasional side trip to Heath Bars. I suppose if I had to, I could eat a Mounds bar, but like most kids who at one time or another overindulge in a candy, mine was Mounds and I got sick on them in third grade. At the time, I liked them almost as much as Milky Ways and one day I decided that my latest book from the library would be more fun to read with a stash of Mounds bars. I bought five - an entire quarter's worth - ate them all, and naturally got sick as a dog. I don't think my mother knew why but maybe the coconut breath gave me away. I steered clear of Mounds bars - and Almond Joy as well - for the next fifty or sixty years. Tom, my late husband, got so sick on candy corn when he was a kid that he couldn't even look at the "little orange teeth" as he called them.

When I started thinking about candy for this article, I was surprised how broad and eclectic my tastes are now ... from the soft New Zealand licorice that Santa brings, to maple sugar candy, to the peach sours at Peterson's Candy in Busti. I'm amazed at how much I love candy yet have to work so hard at staying away from all of it. It doesn't seem right. If God didn't want us to have candy he wouldn't have created chocolate, right? And I think it must have been one of his Celtic saints who invented butterscotch.

I like all those chewy, sugar-coated candies like spearmint leaves and spicy gumdrops, although for some reason I like them all better when they are left out and a little stale - the chew lasts longer.

"Some candy, little girl?" If I had run into that man our mothers all warned us about, I'd have been in deep trouble.

local.title: Transgender woman says ICE tackled her at Rochester airport, held her in men's detention facility
local.summary: A transgender woman from Singapore says ICE agents arrested her at Rochester's airport and held her at an all-men's detention center in Batavia.
local.body:
A transgender woman claims she was unlawfully arrested by ICE agents this week after her flight home landed at the Rochester airport.

The agents shouted her name – Clara Tan – to confirm her identity before taking her into custody, she said. She then was taken to the detention facility in Batavia that only houses men but released hours later after a physical examination confirmed she did not have male genitalia.

"I’ve just had one of the worst 18- hour periods of my life," Tan wrote of the incident on Facebook . "I think it’s an important story to share."

Tan, 33, says four men who identified themselves as Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents approached her around 12:30 a.m. Tuesday as she left the Frederick Douglass Greater Rochester International Airport. She asked if they had a warrant, she said, then attempted to use her phone. That is when she alleges the men tackled and handcuffed her, injuring her left foot.

"I felt pain like you never felt before," she said, "and the next thing I knew, I was on the ground. And I'm thinking, all right, here we go."

ICE did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment.

Tan is originally from Singapore, and came to the United States in 2019 to attend the American Musical and Dramatic Academy in New York. She filed a petition for asylum in 2019, and had a work permit .

She was returning from California, having traveled there for a concert that got cancelled because the Japanese performers could not obtain visas.

local.body: Two Buffalo brothers are turning their love of sports into a way to give back to their community, helping young athletes get the equipment they need to play.Quentin Littleton, a Canisius High School junior, and his younger brother, Grant Littleton, an Olmsted High School freshman, founded We Got Next, a nonprofit organization aimed at supporting young athletes who may not have the resources to afford sports equipment.The brothers recently made their first donation, surprising 9-year-old Killeon Williams with new cleats, gloves and other football equipment after his coach reached out about his needs. local.summary: A 31-year-old Buffalo man is facing multiple felony charges after authorities say he held his pregnant girlfriend against her will for three days and repeatedly assaulted her before she lost her unborn baby.
local.body: A 31-year-old Buffalo man is facing multiple felony charges after authorities say he held his pregnant girlfriend against her will for three days and repeatedly assaulted her before she lost her unborn baby.Christopher Miranda was arraigned Wednesday morning in Buffalo City Court on felony counts of kidnapping, assault and unlawful imprisonment. He is being held at the Erie County Holding Center.According to court documents, Miranda allegedly confined his girlfriend to a room starting on Friday, blocking the door and refusing to allow her to eat.Investigators allege Miranda repeatedly beat the woman and attempted to strangle her multiple times.Early Tuesday morning, police said Miranda allegedly dragged the woman by her hair down 10 steps, then left her outside.The woman, whom 7 News is not identifying to protect her privacy, began bleeding and was taken by ambulance to the hospital. Her unborn baby did not survive.Investigators said the woman was approximately 25 weeks pregnant. Miranda has not been charged directly in connection with the death of the unborn child. In 2019, New York state repealed laws as part of the Reproductive Health Act that made committing an act that causes a pregnant woman to have a miscarriage a crime."She was pregnant, and that is a particularly vulnerable time for individuals when they are pregnant and in an abusive relationship," Catharine Miles-Kania, CEO of the Family Justice Center, said. entertainment.title: Kim Kardashian Says Family Goes Into ‘Lockdown’ to Protect Her Kids When Ye Makes Negative Headlines
entertainment.summary: The reality star discusses her co-parenting relationship with the rapper in new book Citizen Kim .
entertainment.body:
Kim Kardashian activates a “lockdown” mode to protect her four children when negative stories are circulating about her ex-husband, Ye (formerly Kanye West ), or the Graduation rapper is in the midst of a mental health episode.

In Jonathan Van Meter’s Citizen Kim: The Woman Who Created the Future , Kardashian revealed that she shelters her four children with the embattled rapper — North (13), Saint (10), Chicago (8) and Psalm (7) — which essentially means disconnecting them from the outside world.

“My whole household knows what a ‘lockdown’ means if I text it. Like, ‘We’re on lockdown.’ No TVs, just movies,” she explains on page 308 . “No radio, just plug in a phone for music in the car. Not even, like, Sirius XM, because they talk about current events in real time. It’s like, ’They don’t have to be a party to this.'”

While West and the reality TV mogul’s co-parenting relationship is much healthier in 2026, along with how Ye seems to be walking a straight path this year, Kardashian admits in the book she still worries about her ex-husband, who continues to face backlash for his antisemitic hate speech . (The rapper, who has been open about his mental health struggles, placed an ad in the Wall Street Journal in January apologizing for and explaining his actions.)

“Oh, I worry about him all day. All the time,” she admits — which could be a double entendre for West’s 2015 single — on an earlier page. “That’s the father of my kids. I’ll never not worry about him. And that’s a big burden of having kids with someone who you don’t necessarily get along with. My kids would never know that.”

The All’s Fair star continues: “I do everything in my power to forget about all the negative things that happened. I have to be realistic, and my therapist definitely tells me, ‘Your boundaries have to go up,’ but we manage to co-parent without too much conflict. It’s been pretty smooth for a while. I guess because we don’t talk that much.”

Kardashian remains close with members of West’s family and encourages them to spend time with their children.

“I’m really close with his family. I welcome anyone,” she adds. “I tell them all, open-door policy. Anytime you’re in town, come for dinner with us, see the kids as much as you want, take them out, come over and hang out. That’s their family. So I encourage the relationship with their dad so much.”

entertainment.title: Was System of a Down the Defining Artist of the 9/11 Era in 2001? (Greatest Pop Stars Podcast)
entertainment.summary: Our Vintage Almost-Pop Stardom theme month concludes with a look at the biggest alt-metal band of 2001, and how it got intertwined with the greatest American tragedy of the century.
entertainment.body:
As America was reeling from the unthinkable horrors of the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks, the No. 1 album in the country was a chaotic, incredulous and absolutely incendiary alt-metal LP — full of songs that protested war, questioned authority and insisted listeners wake up to the disorder surrounding them. System of a Down didn’t write or record Toxicity with 9/11 or any of the events that followed in mind, but it became one of the timeliest soundtracks for the moment, as the Hollywood quartet of Armenian descent made the unlikely jump to stardom with its confrontational blend of crushing riffs, gorgeous harmonies, off-kilter humor and straight-faced politics. Related Hayden Panettiere's Death Ruled as Accidental, Case Closed: Reports Forrest Frank Sets Release Date for New Album 'The Jesus Generation' J. Cole Reflects on Kendrick Lamar Feud & Confirms He's Not Retiring: 'I'm Not Using That Word at All' Explore System of a Down See latest videos, charts and news

This month on the Greatest Pop Stars podcast, we’ve returned with another mini-series spin-off of our usual Vintage Pop Stardom series, titled Vintage Almost-Pop Stardom. All October, we’ve been welcoming on some of our favorite guests (and one or two first-timers) to look at a quintet of really interesting artists during years in which they brushed against pop stardom, but perhaps never quite got all the way there (at least in this country). This week, we end the series with the brilliant Craig Jenkins of Vulture talking about System of a Down’s whirlwind 2001, where the band became controversial chart-toppers with music and rhetoric that was transfixing at the time, and has only gotten more resonant (and more popular) in the quarter-century sense.

Along the way, we answer all the most pressing questions about 2001 System: What circumstances allowed this thrashy, arty, explicitly challenging form of metal to get in the mix for the top of the Billboard charts? Did the band’s combustibility — and the very different personalities of its four members — end up feeding its music? How much did the Clear Channel Memorandum actually affect the airplay of “Chop Suey”? How do we feel about Serj Tankian’s polarizing “Understanding Oil” essay and how he handled the blowback from it? Was it a big deal for Toxicity to be named SPIN’s No. 1 album of 2001? And perhaps most importantly: Will the band ever record new music again?

entertainment.title: Michael Bay, Benedict Cumberbatch Left Rattled in New Netflix Mockumentary ‘Cunk on Cinema’ Trailer
entertainment.summary: Diane Morgan’s Philomena Cunk poses awkwardly comedic questions to the Hollywood veterans and others about the history of the silver screen in a 6-parter to debut Nov. 15.
entertainment.body:
In her latest incarnation, Diane Morgan as Philomeno Cunk returns as the worst informed person on Hollywood in Charlie Booker’s latest mockumentary for Netflix and the BBC , Cunk on Cinema.

The droll actor is entirely out of her depth sitting across from director Michael Bay , actor Benedict Cumberbatch , composer Daniel Pemberton and in all 23 Hollywood experts as Cunk comedically probes the origins of the silver screen.

“When you’re trying to get inside a character, which hole do you enter by, north or south?” Cunk asks a flustered Cumberbatch at one point in a trailer for Cunk on Cinema . “These, er… are odd questions,” an equally bewildered Bay responds during another interview conducted by Morgan’s clueless interviewer/commentator character. Related Stories TV 'The Diplomat' Renewed for Season 5 at Netflix TV 'The Celebrity Traitors' Ratings Have Never Been Higher. So Why Has This Season Felt Unusually Flat?

That’s apparently the point, as the six-part Cunk on Cinema to debut Nov. 15, also puts on the hot seat filmmakers like Mark Cousins and cinematographer Seamus McGarvey and a host of highly-decorated film critics and academics.

“ Cunk will attempt to demystify it all while sitting in lumpy seats with stale popcorn, asking herself where did cinema come from? And why? What does it want? And why can’t it tell us?” a synopsis from Netflix states, as the documentary-style series promises to cover the whole of cinema from the invention of the movie camera to the introduction of AI tools in filmmaking.

Jim Al-Khalili and Ashley Jackson also return after their collaborations on Cunk on Life and Cunk on Earth. Cunk On Cinema, directed by Al Campbell, is a Pacesetter Production for the BBC, with Netflix to stream the series outside the U.K. and Ireland.

Brooker is joined in the writers room by Ben Caudell, Erika Ehler, Eli Goldstone, Jason Hazeley, Dan Maier, Diane Morgan, Joel Morris, Michael Odewale, Kali Varghese and Sam Ward. Brooker also shares the executive producer credits with Jessica Rhoades, Morgan and Sam Ward.

entertainment.body:
A fourth film in the True to the Game universe is ready for action.

The crime-thriller franchise will return with a fourth installment, as True to the Game: Quadir’s Redemption is set to premiere via Paramount+ on Dec. 15, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. Reprising their roles from the previous chapters include Erica Peeples (Gena Rollins), Columbus Short (Quadir Richards), Vivica A. Fox (Shoog), Iyana Halley (Bria), Starletta Dupois (Gah-Git), Andra Fuller (Jerrell), Kris D. Lofton (Terrell) and Lisa Renee Pitts (Viola Richards). Related Stories Movies 'Ali G: Who Iz I?' Extends Theatrical Run as Amazon MGM Says Movie "Delivered Against Our Goals" (Exclusive) TV Melanie Lynskey to Topline Paramount+ Limited Series 'Mushroom Murders'

True to the Game: Quadir’s Redemption continues the trilogy that centers on Gena (Peeples) and Quadir (Short) attempting to establish their life together amid his complicated ties to the drug world. The new film builds on their journey as a question arises surrounding Gena’s baby that threatens to permanently change their relationship.

Salvatore Sclafani directed the movie from a script by Manny Halley, who executive produces for Imani Media Group.

Adapting Teri Woods’ best-selling 1998 novel, True to the Game kicked off the franchise in 2017 and spawned the sequels Game 2: Gena’s Story (2020) and True to the Game 3 (2021). The first three titles will be available for streaming exclusively on Paramount+ on Dec. 1.

During an interview with SideWalks timed to the third movie’s release, Short recalled his initial connection with the premise of the franchise. “What really drew me to the role was the love story, the vulnerability and being true to the game,” the actor explained. “Vivica [Fox’s] character, Shoog, and my character, the loyalty between them — that’s being true to the game. When love comes in, it changes things.”

entertainment.title: Janelle James to Host 2027 Critics Choice Awards
entertainment.summary: It's a switch-up from the last four years when Chelsea Handler was the emcee for the evening.
entertainment.body:
Janelle James will host the 2027 Critics Choice Awards , taking over from Chelsea Handler who was the emcee of the evening for the last four years.

“For over three decades, the Critics Choice Awards have been the place where the conversation about the year’s best work really takes off — and who better to host a show about the best of TV and film than one of the very best in the business?” CCA CEO Joey Berlin says. “We are so honored to have the incredible Janelle James join us to host this year’s Critics Choice Awards.”

James is an award-winning actress and comedian, best known for her role as Ava Coleman in ABC’s comedy series Abbott Elementary . She has garnered five consecutive Emmy nominations for her performance, as well as Critics Choice, Independent Spirit and Gotham Awards nominations. She won an NAACP Image Award in 2023 and 2026, with nominations in 2024 and 2025.

Her first hour-long stand-up special, Janelle James: How Romantic , will debut on Netflix on Nov. 10. Additional film and TV credits include Black Monday and Apple TV’s Central Park , as well as a role in the feature film One of Them Days . She is also co-writing and executive producing a new Hulu comedy titled Rock City.

The 32nd annual Critics Choice Awards will take place this year on Jan. 3, 2027 at The Barker Hangar in Santa Monica, California. The telecast will air live from 7 p.m. to 10 p.m. ET/4 p.m. to 7 p.m. PT. Nominations in both the film and television categories will be announced on Dec. 4.

entertainment.summary: Charlamagne tha God and The Breakfast Club also weighed in.
entertainment.body:
Nicki Minaj is facing backlash for her comments about New York’s Gov. Kathy Hochul, whom she called “evil” in a rant on X on Wednesday night (Oct. 28).

The rapper began with a characteristically blunt post weighing in on her home state’s fast-approaching gubernatorial race, writing , “Kathy Hochul is an evil woman” and advising that the “Democratic Party should forfeit her seat because even if she wins, she will be of great consequence to them.”

“Downward spiral for her,” Minaj continued. “She will not escape God’s wrath. She did not denounce evil when she had the chance.”

The hip-hop star — who was born in Trinidad and Tobago but grew up in Queens, N.Y., from the age of 5 — followed up with an all-caps response to a video she reposted of Hochul’s controversial 2024 remark that there were “Black kids growing up in the Bronx who don’t even know what the word ‘computer’ is,” something she apologized for that same day. “I misspoke and I regret it,” the politician said at the time.

“HOW MUCH MORE DO YOU NEED TO SEE & HEAR FROM THEM?!!” Minaj wrote of the two-year-old incident. “HOW DARE YOU AS BLACK PEOPLE VOTE FOR THIS VILE WICKED CURSE OF A WOMAN? HOW DARE YOU AS CHRISTIANS?! SHE STAYS SILENT ON HARM BEING CAUSED TO THE INNOCENT & THIS IS WHAT SHE THINKS OF YOUR CHILDREN!”

Minaj also reposted a video of Hochul addressing Black congregants at True Bethel Baptist Church in 2025 about her inflation rebate initiative, joking : “Don’t stop by the liquor store, OK? Buy something for the kids — buy them some food. Sometimes I have to stop by the liquor store, too. I understand.”

“So not only does she keep horrible company & laugh at the demonic things her friends do behind the scenes to people who aren’t as politically powerful…Dear God, help us,” the hitmaker wrote of the remark, which the church’s bishop defended at the time as being “in [the] context” of his sermon that day.

The posts come as Minaj has been helping Donald Trump rally for Republican candidates in this year’s midterm elections. In addition to urging followers to vote for Bruce Blakeman in his race against Hochul, she recently appeared at the president’s rally in Michigan, where he invited her to stand up for the crowd and show off her “beautiful a–.”

entertainment.body:
As she gears up to kick off her VIVA LA LISA residency at the Colosseum at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas on Nov. 12, BLACKPINK ‘s LISA sat down with Jake Shane on his Therapuss podcast on Thursday (Oct. 29) to talk first night jitters, working with Rosalía and how she went from never hearing of Labubu dolls to helping to launch a worldwide phenomenon and being fully overwhelmed by the adorably ugly collectible plushies. Related Hayden Panettiere's Death Ruled as Accidental, Case Closed: Reports Forrest Frank Sets Release Date for New Album 'The Jesus Generation' J. Coming off of her 2026 MTV VMA win for best pop for “Dream” from her debut solo album, last year’s Alter Ego , LISA said the boost she got from snagging her own Moon Person and debuting her single “SaWaDiKa” at the show amped her up for the Sin City run. “Now I’m like, ‘OK, I’m looking forward to my residency,” she said, confessing that she was having butterflies about the residency before her VMA performance. “I was so nervous,” she said as she’s gearing up for intense rehearsals for the six-show run that kicks off next month.

“SaWaDiKa,” which debuted at No. 69 on the Billboard Hot 100, appears on LISA’s recently released six-track Press Play EP. The singer said it made perfect sense as the first single from the EP because the phrase is the “first thing you say when you say ‘hi’ to people” in Thailand and it fits with the influence of her home country on the album.

The 29-year-old singer/actress said she spent six or seven months in Thailand reconnecting to her roots — enjoying the food, friends, family and weather — after living in Korea since she was 14. “It feels so good to be back home. Home there. Real home,” she said. “So, when we’re doing this EP, we’re just like, ‘OK. I have so many, inspiration from my hometown.'”

That included putting one of the nation’s ubiquitous three-wheeled tuk-tuk motorized rickshaw’s in the “SaWaDiKa” video and filling her mood board with “so many” Thai-inspired ideas. “And then we’re always talking ‘oh, what if we put a Thai sound and mix with a pop sound?,'” she added about the EP’s closing track, the Britney Spears-like burner “Sweat,” which features a mix of sultry beats and Thai guitar.

Speaking of Spears, LISA said she was obsessed with the “Gimme More” singer as a kid thanks to a cousin who was a huge Brit booster. She listed off “Toxic” as one of her favorite Britney songs, as well as the 2008 Circus album, which featured the title track single, as well as “Womanizer,” “If U Seek Amy” and “Radar.”

entertainment.title: Tate McRae’s ‘Housewife’ Debuts at No. 1 on Streaming Songs Chart
entertainment.summary: It’s the pop star's second No. 1 and first as a lead act.
entertainment.body:
Tate McRae reaches No. 1 on Billboard ’s Streaming Songs chart for the first time as a lead act, bowing atop the Oct. 31-dated tally with “Housewife.”

In the week ending Oct. 22, the song earned 22.9 million chart-eligible streams in the United States, according to Luminate.

McRae led Streaming Songs once before, as the featured act on Morgan Wallen ’s “What I Want.” The tune reigned for six weeks in 2025. Related Hayden Panettiere's Death Ruled as Accidental, Case Closed: Reports Lars Brandle

McRae’s previous best as a lead act was “Tit for Tat,” which peaked at No. 2 in 2025. She first reached the survey in 2020 when “You Broke Me First” peaked at No. 29, while her first top 10 followed in 2023 via “Greedy” (No. 6).

“Greedy” takes over the No. 1 spot on Streaming Songs from Ella Langley ’s “Choosin’ Texas,” which equaled Mariah Carey ’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You” mark for the most weeks at No. 1 on the chart in its 13-year history on the Oct. 24 ranking, logging its 26th week atop the list. “Choosin’ Texas” appears at No. 4 on the latest chart via 20 million streams, up 1%.

Concurrently, as previously reported , “Housewife” debuts at No. 2 on the multimetric Billboard Hot 100 , her highest charting song as a lead act, surpassing the No. 3 peaks of “Greedy” and “Tit for Tat.” She boasts one No. 1, a one-frame rule by Wallen’s “What I Want.”

“Housewife” is expected to be the lead single from McRae’s fourth studio album, which does not yet have a release date. Its predecessor, So Close to What , debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 dated March 8, 2025, and has earned 2.8 million equivalent album units to date.

entertainment.body:
Artist management and entertainment company Neon Coast has named Nikki Boon as chief creative officer, expanding her role to lead creative oversight and direction, as well as international strategy, spanning Neon Coast’s full management roster.

Neon Coast’s roster includes Kane Brown , Nightly, Randall King , Restless Road and Julia Cole.

Boon has been with the company for a decade, working with country music hitmaker Brown and indie alt-pop group Nightly. To date, Brown has earned 12 No. 1 songs on Billboard’s Country Airplay chart and has earned RIAA Diamond certification for the songs “Heaven” and “What Ifs.” Boon has also been instrumental in propelling the Neon Coast roster globally. Nightly will tour Asia and Australia in January 2027, including stops in China, Japan, Singapore, Sydney and Brisbane.

Boon was highlighted as one of five Executives on the Rise in Billboard’s 2026 Country Power Players issue.

“Nikki’s creative thinking is second to none. She has a passion for our artists that you can feel in every conversation she has,” Martha Earls , founder and owner of Neon Coast, said in a statement. “Nikki dreams bigger than anyone I know and has the rare ability to take an idea beyond the unexpected and see possibilities others can’t imagine. Bringing that vision, creativity, and unique perspective to every artist on our roster is one of the greatest ways we can invest in their success.”

“I’m so grateful to Kane, who showed me from his earliest days on the road how powerful a real connection with fans can be, to Nightly, who taught me every angle of what it takes to be an independent artist today, and to Martha Earls, who has always encouraged me and our whole team to dream big, chase ideas and go after our own big wins,” Boon added. “In this new role, I’m excited to support each artist’s manager, building on what they’ve already created and finding new ways to connect with fans at home and around the world.”

entertainment.title: Mekai Curtis Looks Ahead to ‘Power: Origins’
entertainment.summary: The 'Raising Kanan' star shares insights into the next series in the hit Starz franchise, the prequel that has already wrapped filming.
entertainment.body:
Logo text At the start of the final season of Powerbook III: Raising Kanan , boss Sascha Penn told The Hollywood Reporter the “whole reason the series exists is to deconstruct Kanan as you met him in Power and explain how he became who he became.”

Given Kanan’s big presence in Power , it’s only natural that Kanan plays a big role in Power: Origins , which is the next series in the franchise that Penn is also spearheading. So far, most of the reports about the show largely regard it as the genesis of Tommy Egan and James “Ghost” St. Patrick, conveniently ignoring that it’s also a continued look at Kanan and his evolution beyond Raising Kanan . So while young Ghost and Tommy, played by Spence Moore II and Charlie Mann, respectively, keep getting all the buzz for the highly anticipated prequel series, Mekai Curtis is far from done as Kanan Stark. Considering Kanan didn’t die until deep into the next-to-last season of Power , there’s a lot for him to do, especially since the original series hints at a much closer relationship between the three in the very beginning. Related Stories Music Skilla Baby Won't Be Stopped TV Patina Miller and 'Raising Kanan' Boss Sascha Penn on Closing Their Tragic Chapter in the 'Power' Universe: "This Ending Always Made Sense to Me"

Kanan Stark is not the role a young actor previously known for voicing Zack Underwood in Disney’s Milo Murphy’s Law , and also playing Fish Fisher in Disney XD’s Kirby Buckets , typically lands. When Raising Kanan debuted July 21, 2021, Curtis was roughly three months shy of his 21st birthday. After five seasons, however, there’s no denying that Curtis has made it his own.

Confirming Kanan’s strong presence in Power: Origins with THR , Penn praised Curtis’ work: “What Mekai has done on Kanan is spectacular. He’s taken this this guy from a wide-eyed kid to somewhat of a shaded, grizzled veteran. Working with Mekai is truly one of the joys of my career. You can throw anything at him. His performances are incredibly nuanced and layered. I think he’s one of the best young actors working today, hands down.”

Tony winner Patina Miller, who starred as Kanan’s mother Raquel “Raq” Thomas, recalled the big impression Curtis made on her during their first chemistry read. “I saw the hunger. I saw his ability. I saw what he would do with this role,” she says. “I saw someone not afraid knowing he had big shoes to fill. He took it and welcomed it with open arms, and this shit is not easy.
