entertainment.title: Naomi Ritz, Costume Designer and Widow of Harry Ritz of the Ritz Brothers, Dies at 87
entertainment.summary: The daughter of a vaudevillian, she was married to the youngest member of the wacky comedy team for two decades.
entertainment.body:
Naomi Ritz, an artist, costume designer and widow of comedian Harry Ritz of the Ritz Brothers, has died. She was 87.

Good friends with Frank Sinatra , Ritz died Aug. 31 at her home in Pinyon Crest, California, her daughter Janna Ritz Taninbaum announced.

Naomi and Harry married at their Beverly Hills home on Nov. 21, 1965 (she was his fourth wife), and she traveled with her husband, made costumes for him and humorously described herself as his valet. They spent lots of time during the early years of Caesars Palace in Las Vegas and were together until his death in March 1986 at age 78. Related Stories Movies Barbara Barrie, Actress in 'Breaking Away,' 'Company' and 'Barney Miller,' Dies at 95 General News Dolores Huerta, Influential Labor Leader, Feminist and Civil Rights Icon, Dies at 96

The youngest and last surviving member of the Ritz Brothers, Harry, with his brothers Al and Jimmy — their real last name was Joachim — made up a zany comedy team whose celebrated career stretched more than 50 years, from vaudeville and Broadway and Fox and Universal films to nightclubs, television and Vegas.

Sid Caesar once called Harry “the funniest man of his time,” and in a 1985 interview, Mel Brooks said: “In my mind, the word ‘genius’ should be reserved for one person — Harry Ritz.”

Naomi Leon was born in Hollywood on May 31, 1939. Her father, Freddie, was a bandleader during World War II with roots in vaudeville, and her mother, Zare, was an independent businesswoman. Her folks eventually operated a prop warehouse that served the film industry.

She grew up in Vegas in the early 1950s and came of age among the hotels, theaters, nightclubs, performers and musicians in town. She first met Harry through her dad, who knew him through their vaudeville-era circles.

For about 30 years, she made her home in Pinyon Crest, a mountain retreat near Palm Desert that was built by Sinatra in 1970 as a private escape for family and friends. He dubbed her home “Villa Maggio” as a tribute to Pvt. Angelo Maggio, the character he portrayed in his Oscar-winning turn in From Here to Eternity (1953).

entertainment.title: Hollywood’s Hottest New Event: the Airbnb.org Gala?
entertainment.summary: Charlize Theron, Matthew McConaughey, Zoe Saldaña, Joaquin Phoenix, Cynthia Erivo and Charli xcx all came out to the inaugural event, hosted by Jimmy Kimmel on Wednesday night.
entertainment.body:
A hot new gala has entered the Hollywood events scene, from a slightly unexpected source.

Airbnb .org — the nonprofit arm of Airbnb that offers free, temporary housing to people in need — threw its first-ever gala on Wednesday night, featuring a top-tier guest list at Los Angeles’ Milk Studios. Jimmy Kimmel hosted the evening as A-listers including Charlize Theron , Matthew McConaughey, Zoe Saldaña, Cynthia Erivo, Charli xcx , Joaquin Phoenix and Rooney Mara, Sienna Miller, Greta Lee, Serena Williams, Elizabeth Banks, Jessica Alba, Tracee Ellis Ross, Paul Bettany, Joshua Jackson, Ava DuVernay and Demi Lovato were all in attendance. Related Stories Movies Elle Fanning, Mckenna Grace and Kieran Culkin Get Very Candid About Joining 'The Hunger Games' Universe Lifestyle Art of Elysium Gala to Celebrate Rock Photographer Henry Diltz

The event was timed to Airbnb.org’s new initiative where Airbnb will donate a portion of its revenue from every stay to its nonprofit, which will help provide $500 million to Airbnb.org over the next five years. This is all towards the goal of providing 1 million nights of free housing annually and expanding its support beyond disaster response to families traveling for medical care, survivors fleeing domestic violence and more. Since its founding in 2020, Airbnb.org has provided 1.6 million nights of free emergency housing worldwide and responded to more than 200 disasters in 2026 alone.

“We wanted to do a celebration, a gala to really get the word out and let people know that we’re here to help and we want to be able to keep housing more people,” Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky said of arranging the big night, teasing that with the star-studded group of guests, “we mostly do housing but we have a really good team that can get a good turnout together.”

Kimmel got the evening going with some classic Airbnb humor, teasing that at the event “we have some ground rules. Quiet hours start at 10 p.m.; if you use dishes, please bring them to the sink. No pets are allowed unless they’re service animals, which we know none of them really are. And no sitting naked on the furniture or on Chef José Andrés,” who curated the gala’s dinner menu.

The host also joked, “At the end of the show, you’ll have 14 days to post a review of your experience tonight. Please be generous, I hope it’s positive.” Theron made a brief appearance on stage to speak about the domestic violence element of the housing initiative, noting, “if you’ve ever sat down with a survivor of domestic violence, you’ll know that somewhere to stay isn’t just a small thing, it’s actually everything. Because one of the hardest parts of leaving is not just deciding to leave, it’s having somewhere to go,” adding, “the key to a door is not charity, it is the foundation that everything else is built on.”

entertainment.title: Earl Barret, ‘Too Close for Comfort’ Writer and Producer, Dies at 94
entertainment.summary: He also worked on ‘Bewitched,’ ‘Get Smart,’ ‘The Andy Griffith Show,’ ‘The Governor & J.J.’ and ‘See No Evil, Hear No Evil’ and came up with the villain King Tut for ‘Batman.’
entertainment.body:
Earl Barret, the veteran comedy writer who co-developed the Ted Knight-starring Too Close for Comfort and worked on more than 30 other series, including Bewitched , Get Smart , Batman and The Andy Griffith Show , has died. He was 94.

Barret died Oct. 22 of natural causes at his home in Sherman Oaks, his daughter, J.K. Barret, announced. He was a “lifelong learner with a keen, curious mind and a gift for impeccable comic timing,” she said.

The Ohio native also wrote for My Favorite Martian , My Three Sons , My Mother the Car , I Spy , The Wild Wild West , Julia , The Bob Newhart Show , Sanford and Son and Welcome Back, Kotter . Related Stories Movies Elke Sommer, Actress in 'A Shot in the Dark' and 'The Prize,' Dies at 85 Movies Barbara Barrie, Actress in 'Breaking Away,' 'Company' and 'Barney Miller,' Dies at 95

He and longtime writing partner Arne Sultan developed, wrote and produced Too Close for Comfort , which was based on the British sitcom Keep It in the Family , created by Brian Cooke.

The American adaptation, which ran for six seasons (1980-87) on ABC and in syndication, revolved around Knight’s Henry Rush, a cartoonist who works out of the San Francisco home he shares with his wife (Nancy Dussault) and adult daughters (Deborah Van Valkenburgh, Lydia Cornell).

Barret and Sultan first worked together on the 1969-70 CBS comedy The Governor & J.J. , starring Dan Dailey and Julie Sommars. They continued with NBC’s The Partners (Don Adams’ first series after Get Smart ), CBS’ The Sandy Duncan Show , ABC’s Holmes and Yoyo and The New Odd Couple and the CTV’s Check It Out (Adams starred on that one, too).

The pair also were among the credited writers on the 1989 feature See No Evil, Hear No Evil , directed by Arthur Hiller and starring Richard Pryor and Gene Wilder .

An only child, Barret was born on Oct. 17, 1932, in Canton, Ohio. His parents, Aurel and Mary, who owned a confectionery store, got him tap dancing and violin lessons as a youngster before the family came west, and he graduated from Hollywood High School and Los Angeles City College.

entertainment.title: How Bill Paxton’s Son Took Over His Father’s Role in a Western 35 Years in the Making
entertainment.summary: Starring Malcolm McDowell, the quiet comedy gem ‘Last Train to Fortune’ arrives on VOD Nov. 6, with James Paxton taking on the outlaw role originally intended for his late father.
entertainment.body:
Malcolm McDowell is not known for his cheerier side — at least not in the roles he plays on screen.

The screen legend, 83, became a star in Stanley Kubrick’s pitch-black A Clockwork Orange (1971). He later got swept up in the sword-and-sandal sordidness of Caligula (1979). More recently, he played Dr. Loomis in Rob Zombie’s Halloween films.

So audiences may be surprised about his latest turn, playing a cheerful educator in the Old West with an affinity for the literary classics. The film is Last Train to Fortune , and its journey to VOD on Nov. 6 marks the end of a 35-year effort to bring the Western comedy to the screen. Related Stories Movies 'Psycho Killer' Review: Georgina Campbell and Malcolm McDowell in Gavin Polone's Inane Slasher Pic Movies "Failure Is Not an Option": An Oral History of 'Apollo 13'

He originally planned to make the film in 1991 opposite Bill Paxton , who would have played the outlaw who agrees to safely accompany McDowell’s character to his new post.

At the time, Lindsay Anderson, who gave McDowell his breakthrough role in 1968’s if…. , was attached to direct. But Anderson died in 1994. In 2017, McDowell suffered another shocking loss when Paxton died following heart surgery.

“I talked to him two days before he went in and he said, ‘Oh, it’s a routine thing,’” McDowell recalls of his last conversation with Paxton. “I mean, it was terrible. It was just terrible.”

It was veteran producer Brad Wyman, the producer of the 2003 Charlize Theron film Monster , who suggested reviving the film. McDowell still thought the script, by Michele Rifkin, held promise — and pitched James Paxton, Bill’s son, for the part meant for his late father.

The three sat around a kitchen table and took a crack at a read — and James proved to be an inspired choice. The screenwriter’s son, Adam Rifkin, directs.

entertainment.title: Usher & Chris Brown Bring R&B to No. 1 on Monthly Boxscore Report
entertainment.summary: The R&B Tour was the highest-grossing and best-selling tour of September.
entertainment.body:
Since Billboard launched the monthly Boxscore charts in 2019, all types of acts have been No. 1 on the Top Tours chart. Men ( Elton John was first in February 2019), women ( P!nk followed the next month) and mixed-gender groups ( RBD in November 2023); stars of pop, rock, R&B, country, Latin, rap, K-pop, and more. Solo artists and collectives – vocal groups like BTS and Spice Girls , bands like The Rolling Stones and Coldplay , and institutional touring ensembles like Trans-Siberian Orchestra . But in its 75th edition, ranking the biggest touring acts of September 2026, for the first time, co-headliners top the chart. Related Hayden Panettiere's Death Ruled as Accidental, Case Closed: Reports Lars Brandle

According to figures reported to Billboard Boxscore, Usher and Chris Brown ’s The R&B Tour grossed $77.4 million and sold 423,000 tickets across 10 shows in September, making it the highest-grossing and best-selling tour of the month. They are the first pair of artists to share the No. 1 spot on the chart.

Usher and Brown came close earlier this summer, landing at No. 3 in July and August, blocked by BTS and The Weeknd in both months. And in the last seven years, other co-headline duos have come even closer. Def Leppard and Motley Crue ’s double-bill was No. 2 in Aug. 2022, held back by Bad Bunny . Red Hot Chili Peppers and Post Malone were runners-up in Jan. and Feb. 2023, stopped short by Elton John and Ed Sheeran , respectively. And last year, Kendrick Lamar and SZA scored silver in April and May 2025, bested by Coldplay and then by Beyoncé .

September marks Usher’s first month at No. 1, having previously climbed as high as No. 3 as a soloist in Sept. and Oct. 2024. Brown returns to the top exactly one year after last reigning. He scored a record-tying trifecta with three straight months from July-Sept. 2025. Only Bad Bunny and Beyoncé have also been No. 1 for as many consecutive months.

Usher and Brown’s monthly gross and attendance decline from their July and August takes, despite peaking in monthly rank. In July, The R&B Tour earned $98.4 million and sold 538,000 tickets and in August, it brought in $91.8 million and sold 465,000. At $77.4 million and 423,000 for September, they are the first No. 1 since April to gross less than $100 million as the summer stadium season winds down in North America.

The R&B Tour began the month at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif. on Sept. 1 and ended in Glendale, Ariz.’s State Farm Stadium on the 29th. In between, they hit Las Vegas, Arlington, Texas (Dallas-area) and Inglewood, Calif. (Los Angeles). On the Top Boxscores chart, the latter three line up at Nos. 6-8 while the month’s single-night bookends fall just below the 30-position chart.

entertainment.title: Bryan Adams Releases New Trump Protest Song “Lake Ontario”
entertainment.summary: “Empires and regimes, dictators and kings, they all come and go. Lake Ontario is forever,” Adams said on his website after releasing another single targeting the President from his upcoming album.
entertainment.body:
Canadian rocker Bryan Adams has released another Donald Trump protest song, “Lake Ontario,” included as part of his upcoming album, How’s It Goin .

The single, released to YouTube and other social media platforms by the legendary musician, takes aim at the U.S. president, while never naming Trump directly. A music video for the single has Adams standing on a giant rock alongside Lake Ontario, which Trump renamed as Lake America as part of an executive order amid a tariff and trade war with Canada.

“The lake of shining waters is what the Iroquois called her/ It’s the First Nations name, not an executive order,” assert Adams’ lyrics. The star rocker then insists the lake name change was a diversion from a faltering presidency. Related Stories Music Neil Young Sues Trump for Using "Rockin' in the Free World" at Rally: "The Opposite of Everything Donald J. Trump Stands For" General News Nicki Minaj Lands Press Secretary Buzz After Mock Briefing on Air Force One

“Things weren’t going his way in Iran/ So like a baby tossing the toys from the pram/ He may have thought it best to throw a low blow/ And create a real dog and pony show/ But it feels like another distraction,” Adams says in his song’s lyrics. “While the Epstein files are getting traction/ One day they’ll come out and we’ll say ‘There you go’ / And then we’ll all dive into Lake Ontario.”

Earlier this year, Adams released another protest song, “51st State,” timed for Canada Day, the nation’s birthday on July 1. That single release followed Trump making repeated taunts about Canada becoming a 51st U.S. state and launching a cross-border tariff war.

Known for timeless hits like ”Summer of ’69,” ”Heaven” and ”Everything I Do (I Do It for You)”, Vancouver-raised Adams has made a name in the global music scene with his love ballads and rock anthems. He wa s inducted into the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2011 alongside Canada’s Walk of Fame and the Canadian Broadcast Hall of Fame.

His How’s It Goin’ album will be released Nov. 6 via BAD Records. On his website, Adams called the “Lake Ontario” song a response to those looking to rename a perennial cross-border body of water.

“Empires and regimes, dictators and kings, they all come and go. Lake Ontario is forever. This is a song for all the sane people on both shores who know that the current madness will pass, and that Lake Ontario will always be Lake Ontario,” he wrote.

entertainment.title: AMC’s Infamous ‘Dune’ Sandworm Popcorn Bucket Is Back for ‘Part Three’ With New Designs
entertainment.summary: The chain has revealed two buckets for the upcoming film similar to the one that was mocked on 'SNL' and sparked the popcorn bucket wars.
entertainment.body:
Logo text This time, you can get cozy with sandworm popcorn bucket as a couple.

AMC Theatres has revealed follow ups to its most infamous movie tie-in merchandise for Dune: Part Three .

The sandworm popcorn bucket for Part Two , which became an online and retail hit, as well the target of a Saturday Night Live sketch, is back. This time, there’s Sandworm Thumper Collectible along with a Double Sandworm Collectible (the latter a double-worm design for two people sharing).

Such products can significantly boost theater revenue, with collectible buckets often selling for $25 to $50. The Dune: Part Two bucket was credited with setting off a popcorn bucket merchandising frenzy, with Regal selling a bucket last year for The Fantastic Four: First Steps for a whopping $80. Related Stories Business AMC Global Media Chief Communications Officer Georgia Juvelis Exiting Later This Year Movies 'Dune: Part Three' Smashes 'Odyssey' Presale Record at London's BFI IMAX

“The AMC Sandworm popcorn bucket for Dune: Part Two became a viral phenomenon, and we knew that Dune fans would have high expectations for what came next,” said Hank Green, SVP, Food & Beverage, AMC Theatres. “From the moment we started planning the Dune: Part Three collectibles, our goal was to exceed those fan expectations. The Sandworm Thumper and Double Sandworm collectibles take the experience to the next level with designs straight from the movie.”

Both buckets will come with a large popcorn and be available at AMC locations in the United States and at Odeon Cinemas throughout Europe. AMC will also offer other Dune: Part Three collectibles, including drinkware, “mystery keychains,” and a Sandworm plush. The price of the bucket will be announced closer to the film’s Dec. 18 release date.

SNL mocked the previous popcorn bucket’s suggestive design with a musical sketch where a high school student played by Marcello Hernández excitedly tells his friends that he’s going to lose his virginity to the Dune popcorn bucket (at one point singing, “I’m not scared of the teeth in the middle”).

The Dune: Part Two bucket’s creator, Marcus Gonzalez of the Zinc Group, told the Wall Street Journal that sexual innuendo “was definitely not the intent,” and explained, “The worm’s the worm’s the worm.”
